title: Observability: wolfCrypt error codes not logged before errno translation
description: key_import (line 1797), key_generate (line 2190), do_kdf (line 2051), finalize (line 1522), write/update (line 443), sign (line 1233), verify (line 1325), agree (line 1428), and set_iv (line 890) log the raw wolfCrypt return code via %d in the pr_err call. However, these handlers do NOT translate the wolfCrypt code to a kernel errno before logging — they return the wolfCrypt integer directly to userspace, or they translate to -EINVAL/-EIO with no mapping comment. A support engineer cannot distinguish BAD_FUNC_ARG (-173), MEMORY_E (-125), LENGTH_E (-161), or FIPS_DEGRADED_E (-173 region) from the ring buffer alone. Specifically: finalize, write, and set_iv return the wolfCrypt error code directly as the ioctl return value rather than a mapped kernel errno. Returning a wolfCrypt negative number as a kernel errno is incorrect and makes dmesg useless for distinguishing failure classes.
close_reason: False positive: all providers translate wolfCrypt error codes to kernel errno before returning (wolfssl via xlat_err(), kcapi via direct kernel errno). The %d logged in fd.c is already a kernel errno, not a raw wolfCrypt code.
